summary.intent: Work through the Callisto NEXT-WORK plan (parallel lanes of fixes, test debt, refactors and docs), then investigate and optimize `status`/`version`/`release` performance for repos with hundreds to thousands of packages, including whether to adopt gix and git hooks/refs caching.
summary.outcome: Closed the mistakenly opened plan PR #201 and kept the plan local; opened PRs for W2 SYS-RETRY (#202), W1 mixed-routing test (#203), W0 docs refresh (#204), Lane E stack (#205, #206, #208), R3 derive split, and a perf stack (#327 → #328 → #330 plus a many-packages PR). Perf work replaced the history scan with tree-id comparison (net-change semantics), added a reverse identity index and parallel manifest reads, and concluded gix is slower than system git for history walks, so it was not adopted.

repo: Plans/handoff files like NEXT-WORK.md are local-only: kept at .claude/plans/ and excluded via .git/info/exclude; never commit them or open a PR for them.
`just ci` is the gate (90% coverage threshold); agent checks the log's own `exit=` line rather than the background task notification, which only reports the wrapper script exit.
AGENTS.md says no session link in commits/PRs, and ADR changes need user acceptance (e.g. a gix ADR superseding ADR 5; tag-annotation idea would amend ADR 9).
Release harness fakes (gh, cargo, registry) can hide bugs; the plan requires proving fixes with the real tool where a fake could hide the bug.
Tag-ownership manifest read for bare-named tags is a safety check against tags adopted by renamed/removed packages, so it should not be skipped just because the name is currently unique.
Stacked PRs are linked with `gh stack`; a closed PR in a stack blocks relinking, so unstack and relink the open PRs.

Release rerun fix: a package tagged at HEAD now has all operations (registry, tag, GitHub release) observed and stays selected until satisfied; a tag on an older commit settles the version without provider contact.
Template constants in graph init.rs were moved to .tmpl files with insta snapshots committed first to prove byte-for-byte equality.

code.finding: Production git access uses the system binary via this path; there is no gix cache to add today.
IdentityIndex::native_names/native_name/platforms_of scanned the whole name map per package (quadratic, ~12% at 10k packages); fixed with a Mutex-backed reverse index cache that clones to empty.
changedSinceLastTag changed from per-tag history walk to comparing package directory tree ids at tag vs HEAD (net-change semantics); ~22 ms flat in commit count at 400 packages.
SYS-NAPI fix derives napi roster per intent package via `callisto matrix`; macOS bash lacks `mapfile`, so a portable loop is required.
R3 split of the derive function into stage functions was pinned by characterization snapshots and error-path tests; snapshot mutation test confirmed they catch regressions.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, and mutate source to confirm new tests actually fail before trusting a first-try pass.
Measure before extrapolating: earlier perf numbers (6 git processes, 5x commit-hash speedup, gix cache hypothesis) were overturned or withdrawn by realistic fixtures and instrumented probes.
Compare libraries fairly (reuse diff resource cache, repack repos, cold vs warm passes) before concluding; the user's pasted critique led to a corrected gix comparison.
Sandbox rejects inline env, heredocs, compound commands and edits outside the current worktree; use script files and Write/Edit tools, and switch worktrees to edit other branches.
macOS sed one-liners fail; use Edit or Python scripts, and cargo fmt can reflow text so patch scripts must match formatted text.
Verify PR bodies render correctly (literal backslashes in quoted heredocs).

friction: Initially treated PR #201 as the right home for the plan file, wasting a round trip; user objected that it is local tracking only.
Sandbox restrictions (inline env, heredocs, git-mentioning scripts, cross-worktree edits) forced many script-file workarounds.
Could not update .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md from a background worktree session.
Push of the redesign to PR #330 was rejected as non-fast-forward and needed a rebase.
Timing noise (about ±1.1 s) from another compiling process on the machine; early profile missed the start of the run and was misleading.
Several of the agent's own perf claims had to be retracted (6 git processes, 5x commit-hash gain, gix 2 GB cache speedup).
CI failures from existing tests assuming tag-on-HEAD means released, a stray blank line, and a callisto-model lint.
